question: How are synovial joints classified based on how much they can move?
explanation: Synovial joints are classified as diarthrosis because they allow free movement between the bones. [learn more](BMP111_U2_T17#BMP111_U2_T17_h1)

question: Why can synovial joints move much more than other joint types?

options.A: They possess a fluid-filled cavity separating the bone ends
options.B: They lack any form of structural stabilization or tissue support
options.C: They are completely fused together by solid bone tissue
options.D: They are anchored tightly by thick sheets of dense cartilage

explanation: A fluid-filled cavity separates the bones so they do not rub directly against each other during movement. [learn more](BMP111_U2_T17#BMP111_U2_T17_h1)

question: Which part of a joint capsule makes the lubricating synovial fluid?
explanation: The inner layer of the joint capsule is the synovial membrane, which secretes fluid to keep the joint moving smoothly. [learn more](BMP111_U2_T17#BMP111_U2_T17_h2)

question: What kind of cartilage covers the ends of bones in a synovial joint?
explanation: Articular cartilage is made of hyaline cartilage, providing a smooth, cushioned surface that absorbs impact. [learn more](BMP111_U2_T17#BMP111_U2_T17_h2)

question: What is the main job of fluid-filled bursae around a joint?

options.A: To reduce friction between moving structures like tendons and bones
options.B: To supply oxygen directly to the deep layers of bone marrow
options.C: To connect adjacent articulating bone ends securely together
options.D: To manufacture new red blood cells during physical activity

explanation: Bursae act as fluid-filled cushions that stop tendons, muscles, and skin from rubbing harshly against bones. [learn more](BMP111_U2_T17#BMP111_U2_T17_h3)

question: How do tendons and ligaments differ in what they connect?

options.A: Tendons provide passive joint support, whereas ligaments are directly responsible for muscle contraction
options.B: Tendons line the inner joint capsule, whereas ligaments form the outer protective covering
options.C: Tendons connect muscle to bone to produce movement, whereas ligaments connect bone to bone for stability
options.D: Tendons store calcium for bone repair, whereas ligaments absorb shock within the joint cavity

explanation: Tendons pull on bones when muscles contract to cause movement, while ligaments hold bones together to keep the joint stable. [learn more](BMP111_U2_T17#BMP111_U2_T17_h3)

question: Which type of synovial joint allows the widest range of movement in all directions?
explanation: Ball-and-socket joints have a round head that fits into a cup-like space, allowing movement in all directions and rotation. [learn more](BMP111_U2_T17#BMP111_U2_T17_h4)

question: A patient is having trouble bending and straightening their elbow. Which joint is involved?
explanation: The elbow works like a door hinge, allowing bending and straightening along a single plane. [learn more](BMP111_U2_T17#BMP111_U2_T17_h4)

question: What do we call a movement that makes the angle between two bones smaller?
explanation: Flexion decreases the angle between bones, like bending your elbow to bring your hand closer to your shoulder. [learn more](BMP111_U2_T17#BMP111_U2_T17_h5)

question: When someone lifts their arm straight out to the side away from their body, what movement is that?
explanation: Abduction moves a limb away from the midline of the body. [learn more](BMP111_U2_T17#BMP111_U2_T17_h5)

question: Which movement turns the sole of the foot inward?
explanation: Inversion turns the sole of the foot inward toward the middle, while eversion turns it outward. [learn more](BMP111_U2_T17#BMP111_U2_T17_h6)

question: How is circumduction different from simple rotation?

options.A: Circumduction only occurs in hinge joints, whereas rotation is strictly limited to plane joints
options.B: Circumduction combines multiple angular movements into a circular cone shape, whereas rotation spins a bone around its own long axis
options.C: Circumduction involves sliding flat surfaces past one another, whereas rotation bends the angle between bones
options.D: Circumduction moves the body part away from the midline, whereas rotation exclusively brings the limb closer

explanation: Circumduction moves a limb in a circular cone shape using a mix of movements, while rotation is just twisting around a central axis. [learn more](BMP111_U2_T17#BMP111_U2_T17_h6)

question: Which joint condition is caused by an autoimmune reaction that attacks the synovial membrane?
explanation: Rheumatoid arthritis happens when the body's immune system mistakenly attacks its own synovial membranes, leading to painful inflammation. [learn more](BMP111_U2_T17#BMP111_U2_T17_h7)

question: A pregnant client has stiff, painful joints due to the wear and tear of smooth cartilage. What is happening?

options.B: Complete ossification of the synovial cavity
options.C: Fusion of the tendon sheaths around the joint

explanation: Osteoarthritis involves the gradual breakdown of protective cartilage, causing bones to rub together and result in pain and stiffness. [learn more](BMP111_U2_T17#BMP111_U2_T17_h7)
